courses.title: Treat a broken face as ONE face, then sketch on it
courses.objective: After a hole, a boolean or a tilt edit a flat face can be stored as many triangles (you see a triangle in sketch mode). One face groups them, merges them into a single real face when they are flat, and Sketch / Draw / Push-Pull then use the whole face.

steps.title: Start from a plate with a hole
instructions: A plate with a hole is built. Its top face has 2 loops: the outline and the hole.
steps.why: This is the face you will sketch on.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step.

steps.title: Pick the face
instructions: Make sure the filter bar shows ‘One face’ ticked.
Click the top face: every facet that belongs to the same visible face is selected together (the Selection panel shows ‘Face group’ when there are several).
Alt+click picks a single facet if you really want one.
steps.why: One face ON means a face is one click, even when it is stored as many facets.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step.

steps.title: Use One face when facets remain
instructions: If a face still selects in pieces: click a piece, then ‘One face’ on the bar (or AakarFORM › Pick › One face).
Press Grow to add the neighbouring facets, then ‘One face ⏎’.
Tick Flatten only when the facets are slightly tilted and you want a single flat face.
steps.why: Grouping makes Sketch / Draw / Push-Pull see one plane and one outline with its holes. Merging makes the geometry itself one face.

checkpoint.expected: One face feature added to the timeline.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step.

build.note: Use One face when facets remain

steps.title: Sketch on the whole face
instructions: With the face selected click Sketch: the reference edges show the full rectangle AND the hole (no triangle).
steps.why: The sketch plane is the best-fit plane of the whole face; the outline comes from the face's boundary loops.

checkpoint.expected: Sketch shows the full outline and the hole.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step.

steps.title: Draw straight on it
instructions: Press Alt+D, hover the top face and draw a rectangle: it lands on the same plane.
steps.why: Draw in view uses the same whole-face plane.

checkpoint.expected: A rectangle drawn on the face.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step.
